newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Offers stay flat, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Offers stay flat, trade quiet.

text.p: Most soymeal offers were unchanged Thursday in lackluster dealings.
"There's just no real trend in the market right now," said one southeastern U.S. dealer. "It's just all over place."
Scattered export business propped up offers in some rail markets, and one dealer said there were indications that the spot FOB market was offered Wednesday as high as $29.00 over March futures.
Market observers were looking for the National Oilseed Processors to report a strong weekly crushing pace again this week. Estimates ranged from 29.3 to 30.0 million bushels.
Dealers said the pace of the crush was likely to fall in the coming weeks because of seasonal demand weakness and expectations for heavy soymeal exports from Brazil.
Cash sources also noted reports from China that said soymeal overflow stocks at some Chinese ports were becoming moldy and were being offered at very low prices.
